content: Alpine.js (~15KB) provides HTML-attribute-driven reactivity (x-data, x-show, x-for) good for declarative UI state; petite-vue (~6KB, made by Vue core team) is smaller/faster with Vue-style reactivity but a smaller ecosystem/community. Both work via a single CDN <script> tag, no build step. Plain vanilla fetch()+template literals remains viable and zero-dependency for an already-working manual-DOM app; a micro-library mainly pays off if adding many new interactive/reactive widgets.
